pr_body:
Test failures in #74342 have shown that it is possible for a
data frame analytics job to complete and yet for its progress
to appear incomplete.

The reason this may happen is that we persist progress asynchronously
except for when we're marking the task complete. When we mark the task
complete, we make another try to persist complete progress. However,
we skip persistence if the existing progress document is the same.
Those previous fire-and-forget index requests may end up processed
in a different order resulting into overwriting a latter progress
document.

This commit fixes this by making the progress persist calls at
the end of each step wait for the index request to complete. 

Closes #74342
pr_title: [ML] Ensure progress is complete by the time DFA job stops
pr_comment:
I have removed the abortion of storing progress when the task is cancelled as that is causing other test failures.

With regard to the issue of ending up with a progress document if the job gets force-stopped and deleted in quick succession I think the solution is to do what we already do for anomaly detection jobs. When a job is created, we check if there are left over documents matching that job and fail job creation. I think this is an acceptable and consistent way to handle this scenario. I will follow up in a different PR.
@benwtrent Could you take another look please?

review_comment: I think it would be beneficial to log the "persisted progress" object in the `debug` logger. This would probably require a `setonce` or something to grab the `progressToStore` object.
We already log progress if we go on to persist it. I added the progress in the debug logging when we skip storage because it's the same as the previously stored progress.

@dimitris-athanasiou I was actually thinking of logging on line 203: `LOGGER.debug("[{}] Successfully indexed progress document", jobId);`

Which progress document? There is no way to tie in the loglines the progress starting to be indexed and then the same one completing.
Ah, yes. Good point. Will add that too.
